explain.say: See the first step, listen fully? Let your friend finish without cutting in. People calm down when they feel heard. Then, say it back: "So you think the museum is better because it has a planetarium, is that right?" How do you feel when someone really listens to you?

explain.say: Now look at use "I". Say "I see it differently because I love animals", instead of "You are wrong". Talking about your own view sounds fair, not like an attack. Can you turn "That is a silly idea" into an I sentence?

explain.say: See find common ground? Common ground means the things you both agree on. Maybe you both want a fun trip where everyone learns something. Starting there makes the rest easier to solve. What might you and your friend agree on?

explain.say: Last, decide together. You might pick one, mix ideas, take a vote, or simply agree to disagree, which means accepting that you think differently and staying friends. Brilliant! Challenge: try these five steps in your next disagreement and notice what changes.

faq.q: How can I disagree without fighting?
faq.a: Listen fully, say back what you heard, explain your view with "I" sentences, look for common ground, and decide together. Attack the idea, never the person.

faq.q: Why is listening the first step in a disagreement?
faq.a: When people feel heard, they calm down and are more willing to hear you. Listening also helps you understand what they really mean.

faq.q: Why say back what the other person said?
faq.a: Repeating their point in your own words shows you understood and lets them correct any mix-ups before you reply.
asks: Tell me about say it back

faq.a: An I statement explains your own feelings or view, like "I see it differently because...", instead of blaming, like "You are wrong". It keeps the talk calm and fair.
asks: Why say I instead of you?

faq.a: Common ground is what both people agree on, like wanting a fun trip. Starting from shared goals makes it easier to find a solution together.
asks: Tell me about find common ground
What does agree to disagree mean?

facts: Psychologist Carl Rogers suggested in the 1950s that each person restate the other's view to their satisfaction before replying; this is now called active listening.
Many peacemakers and mediators begin talks by finding shared interests, an approach described in the 1981 book "Getting to Yes".
